headline: Hurricanes reach one-year, $3M deal with Alexander Nikishin
take:
Per ESPN, the Hurricanes and restricted free agent defenseman Alexander Nikishin have agreed to a one-year, $3M deal, ending a monthslong standoff. Daily Faceoff adds that he skipped training camp and reportedly asked for a trade after helping Carolina win the Stanley Cup last spring.

The Hurricanes haven't needed him to get started. At 9-2-2 with 20 points through 13 games, CAR owns 60.9% of the expected goals so far this season. Expected goals measures the quality of chances each side creates, so that share says Carolina has controlled play, and the 59% at five-on-five shows it isn't a special-teams mirage. The penalty kill is allowing just 0.52 expected goals per game, which makes it a strength. Our numbers also show goals scored running slightly below expectation (-0.4), so the results aren't flattering the team. If anything, they've been a touch light.

That makes Nikishin's return an addition to a team already playing well, not a rescue. We'd watch how quickly he settles back into the lineup after missing camp, and whether the penalty kill, already strong, gets deeper with him on the ice.
